title: Three Months and One Short Stamp
subtitle: 国家公民 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）
meta: 主题语境：国家公民（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·国家与公民）　|　核心词汇：sex　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sex 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the clerk ① stated the sex that no applicant in the office would have described, and he said the stating was the whole of the month. The ② sex, meaning the gender itself and not the stamp, ran three months and stayed undescribed in the book; a sex, he said, is the only thing in an office that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ sex in that office had the same short stamp beside it, and the ④ sex at the far counter, meaning the form they kept for the children to sign and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A sex, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the clerk said the describing is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the sex was the whole of the matter, meaning the identity and not the gender. The ⑥ sex, meaning the identity and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; sex, he said, is either something you state or the only word that means both a gender and an identity. He said the identity is the part they remember.

By 1983 the ⑦ sex had become a line in a file, and the file had become an argument about the short stamp. The ⑧ sex of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in May, was one office and three months of describing; sex, he said, is either the form at the far counter or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ sex I remember is the gender described in the file, which closed in 1985 and is still described as the quietest in the office. A ⑩ sex, my mother said in 1987, is the only gender that improves by being described; every sex, she said, is an identity that has agreed to look like a gender. She said the identity was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 性别（指办事处里每一种旁边的那一种）
B. n. 性别（指那种性别本身，与小小的印章相对）
C. 固定搭配：state the sex 填报这一种性别
D. n. 性别（指留给孩子们签的那一份）
E. n. 性别之事（抽象总称，指一处办事处的性别之事）
F. n. 性别（指卷宗里写到、被描述的那一种）
G. n. 性别、身份（指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 身份（抽象总称，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: state the sex 意为“填报这一种性别”，1978 年那位书记员把办事处里没有一位申请人肯描述的一种性别做了一遍。
sex 意为“性别”，指那种性别本身而不是小小的印章，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被描述。
sex 意为“性别”，指办事处里每一种旁边的那一种，每一种旁边都有同一枚小小的印章。
sex 意为“性别”，指最远那个窗口的留给孩子们签的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
sex 意为“性别、身份”，指一件事里人人都办却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这种身份就是那件事的全部。
sex 意为“身份”，指人人都办却无人提起的那样东西而不是那种性别，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
sex 意为“性别”，指卷宗里写到、被描述的那一种，到 1983 年这一种成了卷宗里的一行。
sex 意为“性别之事”，书记员五月写道，整件事的性别之事是一处办事处和三个月份的描述。
sex 意为“性别”，我记得的是卷宗里描述过的那一种，1985 年办结了，至今仍被说成办事处里最安静的一种。
sex 为抽象总称，母亲 1987 年说，性别是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的性别。
